audit_groups.finding: The earlier finite section theorem controlled rank. This proof supplies the full arithmetic lattice degree from the retained generic geometric data. It avoids separate controlled integral jet lifts; the generic filtration itself is still a stated geometric input.

The Jensen estimate follows after unitary rotation by averaging coordinate phases and using the exact mean of log|z_1|. Cauchy coefficient bounds on the substituted polytorus and the product formula give H(P)>=-c deg(P), retaining the spherical mean and all embeddings.

The proof uses a K-basis and the fractional ideal of the top exterior power of the actual full lattice. Coefficient integrality gives the correct finite Gauss bound. Hadamard gives the archimedean term with the correct sign; no free integral basis or saturated image is assumed.

Original K-vectors from the short spanning families are selected using graded independence after field extension. Maximal deepest rank, a K-point avoiding finitely many extension-defined hyperplanes, and completion from the original top family give a nonzero determinant with explicit column bounds.

At each good specialization the deep columns are dependent or span the deepest step by maximality. The graded determinant is a scalar times f^b. Cross multiplication at one last-block value and density turn this into a polynomial identity; irreducibility and positive last-block degree yield f^b divisibility.

The monomial sum gives q=delta binomial(T-1,D) and (D+1)b=binomial(T-1,D)(T+D(D+1)). The cofactor degree is y(T-D)-qD(D+1)>=0. The exact intermediate bound and its weaker displayed slope bound retain the rank-defect factor and all logarithmic norm constants.
